transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’m tired all the time. It’s not just normal teacher-at-the-end-of-the-day tired—I can sleep a full night and still have to really push myself through grading, dinner, and getting ready for the next morning.
Has anyone told you that you snore loudly, gasp, or stop breathing at times while you sleep?
No, no one’s ever mentioned that to me. I’m not aware of doing any of that.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I think so. I’m still doing what I need to do for my students and my family, but I’ve pulled back from mentoring, seeing friends, and the creative things I used to enjoy. It just doesn’t feel as worth the effort lately.
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been a couple of weeks, several months, or longer?
It’s been longer than a few months—about two years and two months, I think. It started around when my husband stopped working outside the home and our routine at home changed.

Over these past two years, has your low mood and lack of interest been present nearly every day, or have there been stretches of two months or longer when you felt essentially back to your normal self?
I haven’t really had a stretch where I felt back to normal. It’s been pretty steady for about two years and two months, since my husband stopped working outside the home and things changed at home.
Have you noticed increased sensitivity to cold, unexplained weight gain, or dry skin over the past couple of years?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything like that standing out to me.
Have you noticed feeling unusually short of breath or winded during activities that didn't used to bother you?
I’m not sure—I haven’t really noticed getting unusually winded during activities.
Have you noticed any new or worsening constipation over the past couple of years?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed any real change with that.
Have you noticed any dizziness or lightheadedness, especially when standing up quickly, over the past couple of years?
No, I can’t say I’ve noticed dizziness or feeling lightheaded when I stand up.
Has anyone commented that you look unusually pale, or have you noticed your skin or nail beds looking paler than usual?
No, no one’s said anything like that, and I haven’t noticed my skin or nails looking different.
Over these past two years, have you noticed any significant change in your appetite—either eating much more or much less than usual?
I haven’t really noticed a significant change in how much I eat.
Over these past two years, have you noticed any changes in your sleep—such as trouble falling asleep, waking up frequently, or sleeping much more than usual?
I’m not really sure—I haven’t noticed any particular changes in my sleep.
Over these past two years, have you noticed trouble concentrating or making decisions, like when grading papers or planning lessons?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed any particular problems with concentration or making decisions.
Over these past two years, have you noticed feeling down on yourself, or feeling hopeless about things getting better?

I don’t feel like everything is falling apart, exactly. But I do have a hard time believing I’ll feel lighter again, or get back to being someone who looks forward to things like museums, projects, or just quiet afternoons.

This supports persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) as the primary diagnosis.
